title: UPLB Gold durian (NSIC Dr 11): Fruit and Tree Characteristics
metaTitle: UPLB Gold durian: Fruit and Tree Characteristics
metaDescription: UPLB Gold durian is a durian variety. See its days to harvest, yield, pest ratings, traits and where it grows best. Compare it with others.
excerpt: UPLB Gold is a registered durian variety, also sold or known as NSIC Dr 11. It was registered with the National Seed Industry Council (NSIC) in 2000 as NSIC 2000 Dr 11. Dept. of Horti UPLB bred it. Its record notes a yield of 60 fruits.

heroImage.alt: Young fruit trees planted in straight rows on cleared red soil, the kind of farm where UPLB Gold durian is grown

blocks.text: If you came here looking for NSIC Dr 11, this is the same durian. The facts below come from the NSIC registry kept by the Bureau of Plant Industry, with notes from its seller and farm sources. Compare it with the others in our [durian variety finder](/crop-varieties/durian), or see [every crop variety](/crop-varieties) we list. For the crop itself, read our guide: [Land preparation for fruit trees](/land-preparation/fruit-tree-land-preparation).
Key facts about UPLB Gold durian

blocks.caption: From the NSIC registry and its seller

blocks.text: When does it bear, and how much?

A registered tree variety is described from its mother tree, not from trial plots. The mother tree of UPLB Gold was about 16 years old and about 8 meters tall when it was registered. Its record notes a yield of 60 fruits. It bears every year, with fruit in June July. A grafted or marcotted tree bears years sooner than one grown from seed, and its yield climbs as the tree grows.

anee.io keeps the records of each block of trees, from fertilizer to harvest, with [the growth stages and weather](/features/growth-stages-and-weather) beside them.
Is it resistant to pests and diseases?
The registry gives no pest or disease ratings for this variety. So treat it as untested, and scout every week.
The pests and diseases that hit durian fields most often: [mealybug](/pests/mealybug). Our [pest finder](/pests) and [disease finder](/diseases) help you name what you see.

A fruit of UPLB Gold weighs about 1945 grams, and its shape is oblong. The flesh is yellow and smooth. Its sweetness measured 30 degrees Brix, the share of sugar in the juice. Most table fruit tastes sweet from about 12 Brix up. The edible part is 28 percent of the fruit. The registry notes its fruiting season as June July, bearing annual.
What its seller and farm sources say

items: **Fruit:** Oblong, about 1.95 kg, green, smooth yellow flesh, 30 Brix, about 28 percent edible.

blocks.text: Why farmers know it: a Luzon grown registered durian from UPLB, very sweet at 30 Brix. Check these against what farmers near you have seen, because the same variety can do differently from one town to the next.
Where and when to plant UPLB Gold durian

Davao growers plant named clones such as Puyat and Arancillo for their thick, creamy flesh and small seeds. Plant grafted trees of a known clone, and mix clones for better fruit set. A registered tree variety is a selection from one proven mother tree, and only grafted, budded or marcotted plants carry its traits. A seedling grown from its seed can turn out quite different. So buy from a nursery accredited by the Bureau of Plant Industry, and ask which mother tree the scions came from. Before planting, get the field ready with our guide: [Pagtatanim ng puno](/crops/pagtatanim-ng-puno).

items: Buy grafted or budded plants from an accredited nursery, with the variety name on the tag.
Ask your municipal agriculturist or nearby farmers how it did in your area last season.
Plant a few trees first if the variety is new to your area, before you fill the whole farm.
Write down the planting day, inputs and harvest, so you can compare varieties on your own ground. anee.io keeps these records for you.

items.q: Is NSIC Dr 11 the same as UPLB Gold?
items.a: Yes. NSIC Dr 11 is another name for UPLB Gold, registered as NSIC 2000 Dr 11. Seed sellers use both, so ask for either one.
The record shows a recorded yield of 60 fruits. Your own yield depends on the soil, water, fertilizer and pests on your farm.

items.q: Where can I buy planting material of UPLB Gold?
items.a: Buy grafted, budded or marcotted trees from a nursery accredited by the Bureau of Plant Industry, so you get the true variety. Ask your provincial agriculture office for the nearest one.
